newsitem.title: USA: Minn group spent $1.1mln seeking new stadium-paper.
newsitem.headline: Minn group spent $1.1mln seeking new stadium-paper.

text.p: A corporate-backed booster group supporting efforts for a new Minnesota Twins stadium spent nearly $1.1 million in the past year promoting a new facility, including nearly $112,000 in lobbying the last three months, the Star Tribune reported Wednesday.
Documents filed with a state ethics board show that the Minnesota Wins booster group reported $111,747 for lobbying legislators, the newspaper reported.
Another $1 million was spent on community efforts, according to the organization director, the newspaper said.

The group has collected $1.6 million, has about $100,000 in outstanding pledges, and expects to spend all $1.7 million on the effort to build a new stadium for the American League baseball team, the newspaper reported.

Proposed legislation supporting a new ballpark has moved from preliminary consideration in the Minnesota House and Senate in the current session. Senators stripped public funding from their bill before advancing it, while representatives moved a bill along for further consideration without a recommendation.
Early estimates placed the cost of a new ballpark at from $250 million to $300 million or more if a retractable roof is included in the project.
Twins officials have placed the cost of a new facility at closer to $400 million, plus infrastructure improvements.
